subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a closed skill?
options: It is performed in a predictable, stable environment and is unaffected by surroundings
It is always affected by opponents and the environment
It always uses only small, precise movements
It is always started in response to an external signal
questions.explain: Closed skills take place in a predictable environment and are largely unaffected by external factors such as opponents or conditions.

questions.q: A gross skill is one that involves:
options: Large muscle groups and big movements
Small muscle groups and precise, delicate movements
questions.explain: Gross skills use large muscle groups to produce big, powerful movements, such as a shot-put throw.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of an open skill?
options: A pass in a hockey match
questions.explain: An open skill is affected by an unpredictable, changing environment, such as passing while opponents move around you.

questions.q: A gymnast performs a vault, choosing when to begin and working in a predictable setting. How is this skill best classified?
questions.explain: The environment is predictable (closed) and the performer controls the timing of the start (self-paced).

questions.q: In the SMART principle of goal setting, what does the letter 'M' stand for?
questions.explain: SMART targets should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound, so progress can be tracked.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of setting goals for a performer?
options: To motivate the performer and monitor their progress
To make training last as long as possible
To remove the need for any feedback
To guarantee the performer always wins
questions.explain: Goal setting increases motivation and allows performance to be measured and reviewed over time.

questions.q: A coach sets the target 'get better at football'. Which SMART principle does this target most clearly fail to meet?
options: It is not specific or measurable
questions.explain: The target is vague, giving nothing precise to aim for or measure, so it breaks the Specific and Measurable principles.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the stages in the basic information processing model?
questions.explain: Information is taken in (input), a decision is made, the movement is carried out (output), and feedback follows.

questions.q: The input stage of the information processing model involves:
options: Receiving information from the environment through the senses
Choosing which response to make from memory
Receiving comments from a coach after the action
questions.explain: During input, the performer gathers information from their surroundings using their senses.

questions.q: What does selective attention allow a performer to do?
options: Filter out irrelevant information and focus on the relevant cues
Remember every detail of the environment equally
questions.explain: Selective attention lets the performer concentrate on important information (e.g. the ball) and ignore distractions (e.g. the crowd).

questions.q: During the decision making stage, the performer mainly uses their memory to:
options: Select the most appropriate response to the situation
questions.explain: Decision making draws on memory of past experiences to choose the best response to the current situation.

questions.q: In the information processing model, the 'output' refers to:
options: The muscular movement or action that is performed
The information gathered by the senses
The choice of which skill to use
questions.explain: Output is the physical response, when the chosen movement is sent to the muscles and carried out.

questions.q: A netball player sees a free teammate, decides to pass, then throws the ball. Throwing the ball represents which stage of information processing?
questions.explain: Physically throwing the ball is the muscular action, which is the output stage.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognised type of guidance?
questions.explain: The four types of guidance are visual, verbal, manual and mechanical.

questions.q: Manual guidance is best described as when a coach:
options: Physically moves or supports the performer's body through the movement
Shows a demonstration of the skill
Uses equipment such as a harness to support the performer
questions.explain: Manual guidance involves the coach physically holding or moving the performer's body into the correct position.

questions.q: Mechanical guidance involves the use of:
options: Equipment or aids, such as a float or a harness
questions.explain: Mechanical guidance uses equipment or apparatus to support or shape the movement, for example a float in swimming.

questions.q: Why is visual guidance particularly useful for beginners?
options: It helps them form a mental picture of the skill by watching a demonstration
It relies on their kinaesthetic sense which is well developed
It removes the need to see the whole movement
It always uses complex tactical language
questions.explain: Seeing a demonstration lets a beginner create a clear mental image of what the skill should look like.

questions.q: Knowledge of results (KR) is feedback about:
options: The outcome or result of the movement
How the technique felt during the movement
questions.explain: Knowledge of results gives information about the outcome, such as whether a shot scored or missed.

questions.q: Intrinsic feedback is feedback that:
options: Comes from within the performer through their own feelings and senses
Is always given by a coach or teammate
Can only be received after the event has finished
questions.explain: Intrinsic feedback comes from within, using the kinaesthetic sense to feel whether a movement was correct.

questions.q: A beginner learning to somersault on a trampoline is supported by a coach using an overhead harness and rope. Which type of guidance is this?
questions.explain: Using a harness (equipment) to support the movement is an example of mechanical guidance.
